transcript.text: Welcome, everyone. As you know, I've been asked to restore a worn 1920s community cookbook. It has a detached cover and several loose pages. Before I decide whether to accept the commission and set the final terms, I'd like to hear from everyone — please state any terms, offers, or material constraints you know of. That way we can make sure we're all on the same page before I commit to anything.

transcript.text: I'd like to propose a barter arrangement. Inez, if you'll reattach the cover, resew the loose sections, and make a simple cloth spine, I'll provide twelve archival linen sheets plus $40 in exchange. I'd bring the book Tuesday at 18:00 and collect it Saturday at 16:00.

transcript.text: I'd like to put an offer on the table as well. I've offered Inez $320 cash for a separate two-week restoration of a family recipe ledger, and that offer remains open.

transcript.text: I inspected this cookbook for a local archivist, who confirmed that its brittle acidic pages require wheat-starch paste and Japanese tissue for the loose-page repairs. Ordinary PVA glue should not be used.
